Thought: I need to determine which amino acid residue in topoisomerases facilitates the temporary splitting of DNA strands. Topoisomerases are enzymes that regulate the overwinding or underwinding of DNA by breaking and rejoining DNA strands. Let me think about which amino acid is involved in this catalytic process.

Topoisomerases use a nucleophilic amino acid residue to attack the phosphodiester backbone of DNA, forming a covalent intermediate that allows for the temporary breaking of the DNA strand. This amino acid needs to have a nucleophilic side chain.

Among the options:
A. Aspartate - has a carboxylic acid group
B. Phenylalanine - has an aromatic side chain but not particularly nucleophilic
C. Serine - has a hydroxyl group that can act as a nucleophile
D. Tyrosine - has a hydroxyl group on an aromatic ring that can act as a nucleophile

In topoisomerases, tyrosine is the key catalytic residue that forms a covalent phosphotyrosine linkage with the DNA during the strand breakage process. The hydroxyl group of tyrosine attacks the phosphodiester bond in DNA, creating a covalent enzyme-DNA intermediate that allows for the temporary breaking of the DNA strand.
Final Answer: [ANSWER]D[/ANSWER]
